L0: A procedure for creating held-out task sets used to evaluate agents.
L1: A procedure for creating held-out task sets used to evaluate agents. Weaker task generators, rather than the evaluated agents, produce a fixed number of task specifications or scenarios, each with an executable check or validator withheld from the evaluated agents. Generators cannot observe evaluated-agent traces; the procedure is rerun for each model family or repeated with newly sampled generators and fresh validators, preventing one task-writing distribution from dominating. Tasks are filtered for execution validity and duplicate surface form, human review rejects ambiguous state transitions, and comparisons normalize available-tool counts and instruction length.
L2: This is a procedure for generating task or benchmark sets for evaluating agents, including data-management scenarios. In each run, weaker held-out task generators—not the evaluated agents—produce a fixed number of task specifications, such as 2,160. Every task includes an executable check or validator, but evaluated agents do not receive it. The generators are prevented from seeing evaluated-agent traces. The procedure is rerun for each model family, or later rounds use newly sampled generators and fresh validators, so one task-writing distribution does not dominate comparisons. Generated tasks are filtered for execution validity and duplicate surface form. Human review also rejects tasks with ambiguous state transitions; in one set it rejected 11%, leaving 1,740 tasks. Results are read after normalizing for the number of available tools and the length of task instructions.
